site.name: Crackspread
site.description: The world oil balance, crack spreads and what they mean for trucks, food and flights. Explained like a whiteboard, updated three times a day.

crack.title: Crack-o-meter
crack.sub: Analysts say 'crack spreads are widening' with a straight face. We'll show you why.
crack.explain: A crack spread is what refiners earn for 'cracking' crude into diesel or gasoline. Product price minus crude price. That's it. No, you don't have to blur it, it's just a chart.
crack.footnote: NY Harbor ULSD minus Brent. Other benchmarks (Europe, Singapore) can read higher.
crack.gauge_label: Diesel crack, where it sits in history
crack.percentile: Wider than {pct}% of all trading days since {start}.
crack.table.note: Last {n} data points of the chart. Full history in prices.json.
crack.spread_fact: Side note: Brent trades ${v}/bbl above WTI. The 2015–19 average was ${mean}. Not a typo. A spread.

meth.title: Methodology
meth.formula.diesel: diesel crack = NY Harbor ULSD ($/gal) × 42 − Brent ($/bbl)
meth.formula.gasoline: gasoline crack = NY Harbor gasoline ($/gal) × 42 − Brent ($/bbl)
meth.formula.jet: jet crack = US Gulf jet fuel ($/gal) × 42 − Brent ($/bbl)
meth.series: FRED series: {ids}. Cracks are computed only for days on which every input exists; FRED leaves holidays empty (older files used a dot), and those days are skipped.
meth.benchmark: Max Fisher's whiteboard mentions a ~${fisher}/bbl record diesel crack. Our US benchmark (NY Harbor ULSD minus Brent) reads ${ours}/bbl and peaked at ${max}/bbl on {max_date}. He likely means a different benchmark (European gasoil or Singapore), so his number appears only in the whiteboard explainer, labelled as his estimate with benchmark not specified.
meth.steo: The balance comes from the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO). The current month is an estimate, later months are forecasts, and both get revised every month. That's normal.
meth.updates: The site updates three times a day at about {times} ({tz} time). Scheduled runs can be up to half an hour late.
meth.stale: If a source doesn't answer, we keep the last known value and mark it STALE with its date. We never fill gaps with guesses. Prices count as stale after {prices} h, the STEO after {steo} h, news after {news} h.
meth.history: The chart shows weekly values before {date} and daily values after. The percentile is computed on the full daily history since {start}.
meth.sources_note: Every number on this page carries its source and as-of date in the small print next to it.
